title: Keychain, data protection and secrets
summary: Store secrets (tokens, passwords, keys) in the Keychain, encrypt files with Data Protection, and never ship real secrets inside the app - anything in the binary can be extracted.
body: **In simple words:** The Keychain is an encrypted vault managed by iOS. UserDefaults and plain files are not safe for secrets.

**Accessibility classes (when can the item be read?):** `WhenUnlocked` - only while the device is unlocked (default, safest for foreground use). `AfterFirstUnlock` - after the first unlock since reboot (needed if background tasks need the token). `...ThisDeviceOnly` - not included in backups or moved to a new phone.
**Biometrics:** protect an item with Face ID/Touch ID using `SecAccessControl` (`.biometryCurrentSet` invalidates it if fingerprints/faces change). Use `LAContext` for the prompt.
**Secure Enclave:** a separate chip that can create keys which never leave the hardware (`CryptoKit.SecureEnclave.P256`). Use for signing requests that prove "this device".
**Surprise:** Keychain items survive app deletion. On first launch after reinstall, clear old items if needed (track a flag in UserDefaults, which is deleted with the app).
**API keys in the app are public:** attackers can read strings from the binary. Keep secrets on the server, use short-lived tokens and App Attest.
**Other basics:** hide sensitive screens in the app switcher snapshot, avoid logging personal data, and clear sensitive data on logout.
keyPoints: Secrets → Keychain with the narrowest accessibility class.
`AfterFirstUnlock` if background code needs access; `ThisDeviceOnly` to avoid backup/migration.
Secure Enclave keys never leave the device.
Keychain items survive reinstall; handle stale items.
No real secrets in the binary.

mistakes: Storing tokens in UserDefaults or plain files.
Hard-coding API secrets and assuming obfuscation protects them.
followups: **Is jailbreak detection worth it?** Only as a deterrent; it can be bypassed. Server-side checks and App Attest matter more.
**How do you share a login between the app and an extension?** Keychain access group shared by both targets.
